raw_response:
I am fifty-nine years old, and I have farmed this land in Quzhou for more than forty years. My household has six mu of flat, irrigated land. I finished middle school, so I can read what is written on seed bags and fertilizer sacks, but I trust my own eyes and what the neighbors have proven over the years more than anything else.

This year I will keep all six mu in the wheat-corn rotation. That is what this soil was made for, and it is what my body can still manage. I did think about putting two mu into cotton, because the price can be good, but I am getting older and my back and knees are not what they used to be. Cotton needs pruning and spraying a dozen times or more, and harvesting it by hand across a long season is too much for me to handle alone. Wheat gives us flour for our own steamed buns and noodles, and corn always sells for cash at the village collection point or feeds our chickens. I will not fix what has fed my family for decades.

The winter wheat is already in the ground—I sowed it last October with an improved variety, the kind that yielded reliably for Old Wang next door. I used about thirty jin of seed per mu. Before sowing I rotary-tilled the field, and I laid down one hundred jin of compound fertilizer per mu as basal. Come March, when the wheat turns green, I will top-dress with urea. I will irrigate four times: once before winter, and three times in spring when the north wind blows dry. I will spray for insects twice and for weeds once. If the weather does not play tricks, I expect about one thousand jin per mu.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will plant summer corn immediately without plowing. No-tillage saves diesel and time, and the wheat stubble helps keep the moisture in the ground during the hot months. I will use hybrid seed—one package per mu is plenty. I will spread compound fertilizer at sowing, about eighty jin per mu. The corn will need two irrigations, one in July and one in August if the rains are stingy. I will spray twice for insects and once for weeds. I expect about eleven hundred jin per mu.

That is my plan. It is not fancy, but it is honest work, and I know every step of it by heart.
